metadata.title: Trump says regime change in Cuba is ‘question of time’ after Iran

left: U.S. President Donald Trump suggested that Cuba is close to collapse due to U.S. actions, including cutting off Venezuelan oil supplies critical to Cuba's electricity, causing widespread blackouts and power outages affecting millions on the island.
The Cuban government is experiencing severe electricity challenges characterized by blackouts and fuel shortages amid reduced imports influenced by U.S. sanctions.
Trump indicated that after addressing the situation with Iran, the U.S. would turn its focus to Cuba, expecting the Cuban regime to fall under continued pressure.
Trump claimed the U.S. is in contact with the Cuban government amid escalating turmoil and widespread blackouts caused by fuel shortages and grid failures.
center: At a White House East Room event, Trump said he plans to focus on Cuba after Iran, suggesting negotiations may follow soon.
After U.S. actions cut Venezuelan oil supplies, Cuba faced a fragile power network and a massive December failure in its national electricity grid.

At least five million Cubans rely on electricity for chronic care, PAHO reported 385 health facilities damaged and seven provinces face water shortages, while almost one-in-three Havana households lost power.

On Wednesday, Ecuador declared Cuban ambassador Basilio Antonio Gutiérrez persona non grata, ordering diplomats to leave within 48 hours as regional protests and cancellations of Cuban medical contracts followed.
Trump predicted Cuba would fall and signalled negotiations may follow, saying `Well, it's because of my intervention, intervention that is happening` during a Politico interview.
right: President Donald Trump indicated that the US may focus on Cuba after completing military operations in Iran and mentioned it is only a question of time before Cuban Americans could return to their homeland.
The US has intensified economic pressure on Cuba, including an energy blockade after cutting off Venezuelan oil supplies, worsening Cuba's economic crisis.
Trump praised Secretary of State Marco Rubio's efforts regarding Cuba and suggested the US might pursue significant changes there following the Iran conflict.

Rising tensions include increased anti-imperialist rhetoric and military exercises by Cuban officials amid fears of a US intervention similar to the one in Iran, with a severity of tensions unseen since the 1960s.
